Write TRUE if the statement is correct and FALSE if the statement is not correct. (i) “The Lord said to Cain, ‘Where is your brother Abel?’” shows God’s concern for human life. (ii) Noah entered the ark because he was without sin. (iii) Abraham obeyed God even when he did not fully understand the destination. (iv) The Israelites received the Ten Commandments before crossing the Red Sea. (v) “Man shall not live by bread alone” teaches dependence on God. (vi) Samson’s strength was physical rather than spiritual. (vii) Saul admitted his sin immediately without excuses. Page 5 of 7 Find this and other free resources at: https://maktaba.tetea.org Find this and other free resources at: https://maktaba.tetea.org (viii) David’s repentance restored his relationship with God. (ix) Prophets were mainly fortune tellers for kings. (x) The exile was a result of long-term disobedience. (xi) “Choose this day whom you will serve” reflects Israel’s freedom of choice. (xii) Moses saw the Promised Land but did not enter it. (xiii) The judges ruled Israel in a continuous peaceful period. (xiv) God used both blessings and punishment to guide Israel. (xv) Obedience in the Bible is often linked with life and prosperity. (xx) The Law was given to replace faith with rules.

Give short answers to the following questions. (i) Explain two reasons why God accepted Abel’s offering but rejected Cain’s. (ii) State two purposes of God’s covenant with Abraham. (iii) Give two reasons why the Israelites complained during their journey in the wilderness. (iv) Explain two ways in which Moses showed leadership during the Exodus. (v) State two lessons learned from the fall of Jericho. (vi) Give two reasons why Saul was rejected as king. (vii) Mention two qualities that made David a successful leader. (viii) Explain two roles played by prophets in Israel. (ix) State two reasons why the Law was important to Israel’s life in Canaan. (x) Mention two benefits of repentance according to biblical teaching. Answer the following questions. (i) “As for me and my household, we will serve the Lord.” Joshua 24:15 (a) Who spoke these words? (b) To whom were the words addressed? (c) What situation led to this declaration? (d) State two lessons modern believers can learn from this statement. (ii) The fall of man is recorded in Genesis 3. (a) Explain God’s punishment to the serpent. (b) Explain God’s punishment to the woman. (c) Explain God’s punishment to the man. (d) What does this passage teach about obedience and responsibility? (iii) “The Lord is holy.” Using examples from Moses’ encounter at the burning bush and Israel’s worship practices, explain how God’s holiness shaped Israel’s understanding of worship.
